messages:
maya (Design): uploaded a new frame: https://figma.redwood.example/file/spotlight-flare-ux

maya (Design): idea: instead of vertical keylines i'd like to try a 'spotlight' flare that softly illuminates the heatmap column where RPS jumps > 2.5x. it would nudge attention but be less noisy than hard lines.

ravi (Frontend): interesting. how does spotlight behave with p95 sparkline overlays? ensure p95 remains crisp — maybe spotlight is a low-opacity radial gradient behind the heatmap column.

maya (Design): yep gradient behind. sketch shows 40% radial fade, 8px horizontal spread. p95 stroke sits above. also propose keyboard focusable hotspots for each flare (tab to next burst).

nora (PM): product question: what do we call these in UI copy? "Flares" feels playful; customers might prefer "High-traffic highlights" or "RPS spikes". also need one-line tooltip copy.

leo (Observability): backend: we can emit spike events with severity. recommend naming aligned with telemetry event: "rps_spike". UI label can be friendly. also note sampling: small spikes may be missed at low sampling. we could compute spikes from full ingestion and deliver an events feed.

a11y-bot: accessibility reminder: any non-textual indicator must have an accessible name, keyboard focus, and visible focus ring. Contrast guidance: interactive indicators should meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent background.

ravi (Frontend): for keyboard, each spotlight hotspot should be a button with aria-label like "RPS spike at 12:03, peak 1.2k rps". when focused, show a small panel with details. that also helps screen-reader users.

maya (Design): proposed legend copy: "High-traffic highlights (RPS spikes)". tooltip: "Periods where request rate rose notably above recent baseline." short CTA in onboarding: "Highlights call out sudden changes in traffic to help triage".

nora (PM): prefer explicit: "RPS spikes" in legend, with explanatory secondary text. marketing might rephrase elsewhere. defaults: enabled for new users?

maya (Design): my recommendation: enabled by default, but collapsed in a legend group so users can toggle. add an 'i' micro-tooltip with 'why you see this' linking to docs.

leo (Observability): rendering perf note: gradient per column is heavier than line overlays. Suggest render only aggregated spikes at < 6h zoom. real-time stream should debounce to 1s for live updates.

ravi (Frontend): implementation idea: draw spotlights into a single canvas layer behind heatmap tiles rather than many DOM nodes. simplifies performance and keeps p95 svg on top. will prototype.

a11y-bot: check color-blindness: avoid relying on hue alone. use pattern or subtle hatch for high severity spikes in a11y mode. also ensure focusable elements have at least 3px visible ring or equivalent.

maya (Design): good call. add a faint diagonal hatch for severity-high state when in a11y mode. normal mode: orange-to-transparent radial gradient. provide alt copy: "High-traffic highlight: severity high".

nora (PM): UX question: when clicking a spike, should we auto-snap the time-range picker to a narrow window around the spike? that could help triage but might annoy users who were comparing ranges.

ravi (Frontend): option: ctrl/cmd+click snaps, normal click opens details panel without changing range. or show a 'zoom' affordance in the details panel. less surprising.

maya (Design): agree on non-destructive default. details panel with 'Zoom to spike' button. also include quick links: open traces, logs.

leo (Observability): telemetry will include links: trace_id sample, logs query template. we can populate quick links in the panel. note: trace may be missing if sampling skipped; show 'no traces sampled' message gracefully.

a11y-bot: interactive panel content should be keyboard navigable and labelled regions should use ARIA roles (dialog/region) so screen readers announce context change.

maya (Design): acceptance criteria I'll add to spec: - spotlights render aggregated at low zoom - aria-labelled hotspot buttons - details panel with timestamp, peak RPS, duration, sample confidence - 'Zoom to spike' action separate from click - a11y hatch fallback and focus styles - legend toggle persisted in user prefs

nora (PM): sounds good. timeline: can we ship a small A/B test to 10% to see signal usefulness before rolling wide?

leo (Observability): yep we can gate via feature flag and include telemetry on click-throughs and zooms. will coordinate with backend RFC.

ravi (Frontend): i'll prototype canvas approach and test perf on heavy boards. expect a PR next week.

maya (Design): i'll update Figma with the hatch states and the details panel copy; will also write the microcopy for onboarding. pinging when ready. :sparkles:

ravi (Frontend): :thumbsup:

nora (PM): thanks everyone!
